title: Reading Conversational Tone from KV-Cache Keys
subtitle: Position and Planning-Text Confounds (A Methods Note)
abstract: At four early full-attention layers of Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-distill, cached keys projected on emotion directions move with sequence position and the amount of history (not separated here) far more than with the conversational tone compared. In Experiment 1 the chunk that holds the same neutral probe (and the tail of the previous generated turn) reads +4.61 and +4.65 (cheerful, hostile) after one emotional turn and -1.60 and -3.71 after eight; the gap between arms there is within 0.22 of zero through four turns and +2.11 at eight (p = 0.056, uncorrected), where that chunk's generated text differs between arms. In Experiment 1 and the initial study the history read includes the model's own planning text, which often uses a tone word (in Experiment 1, 59 of 135 hostile-arm and 54 of 135 cheerful-arm excerpts): the stored assistant turns open with it, except where the chat template stripped the planning. Where compared arms differ in text at the read site, as in Experiment 1 at every read site and in Experiment 2 at the measured turn, a comparison cannot separate history from that text, so Experiment 2's contrast-overshoot and uncertainty-scar patterns (the first version's headlines) are not supported as effects of history. Two comparisons are matched in position. In the initial study one topic's two reruns per arm are length-matched, and their gap at the probe is +0.08 against rerun SDs of 0.23 and 0.12 (one topic, one script, undocumented read site). Hostile against cheerful persona prompts, the one comparison length-matched on every probe, moves the valence projection (d_av = -0.68) consistently on five probes, too few to reach p < 0.05 by permutation; its script is not shipped and its read site is undocumented. A test of whether these keys accumulate tone needs fixed (teacher-forced) neutral assistant turns, comparisons matched in position and length, and behavior as ground truth.
